cards.q: What is multicast routing and what is its core rule?
cards.a: Multicast routing forwards copies of a packet away from the source along a distribution tree. The core rule is RPF (Reverse Path Forwarding): a packet is forwarded only if it arrived on the interface the unicast table would use toward the source.

cards.q: Why does the RPF check make the tree loop-free?
cards.a: Because only packets arriving on the interface the unicast route uses toward the source are forwarded, traffic always travels away from the source, which prevents loops.

cards.q: How does multicast decision-making differ from unicast?
cards.a: Unicast forwards toward the destination address; multicast forwards away from the source using RPF, which is based on the source. PIM reuses the existing unicast RIB for RPF instead of building a separate multicast topology.

cards.q: What do (*,G), (S,G), OIL, and flags mean in an mroute table?
cards.a: (*,G) is an any-source shared tree entry for the group, (S,G) is a source-specific shortest-path entry, OIL is the outgoing interface list, and the flags record the RPF check result. A correct (S,G) with a proper OIL means the tree is being built.

cards.q: What is MBGP and which SAFIs does it use?
cards.a: MBGP is BGP that carries NLRIs for multicast; SAFI 1 is unicast and SAFI 2 is multicast. It provides a separate multicast RPF path so the RPF path may differ from the unicast path.

cards.q: Which tools handle inter-domain multicast, and what is each for?
cards.a: MBGP provides multicast reachability, MSDP provides RP peering and source discovery, PIM forwards between domains, and SSM (IGMPv3 plus PIM-SM) simplifies inter-domain by removing RP and register complexity.

cards.q: How do you mitigate RPF asymmetry and prevent loops in multicast design?
cards.a: Use MBGP or a default route to correct RPF asymmetry, peer PIM per link, scope with TTL or boundary, and always enforce RPF to avoid loops.

cards.q: Which commands verify multicast routing and RPF?
cards.a: show ip mroute and show ip mroute count show the tree, show ip rpf <IP> verifies the reverse path, and show ip pim interface plus debug ip mpacket help with diagnosis.

cards.q: Multicast packets are being dropped by RPF; what do you check?
cards.a: Whether the inbound interface matches the source-facing RPF interface; verify with show ip rpf.

cards.q: Multicast is not forwarding or takes the wrong path; what do you check?
cards.a: An empty OIL means no forwarding, check show ip mroute count; a wrong path usually means unicast asymmetry, fix with MBGP.

cards.q: State the RPF forwarding rule exactly.
cards.a: Forward a multicast packet only if it arrived on the interface the unicast table would use toward the source; otherwise it is an RPF failure and the packet is dropped.

cards.q: A packet for a source arrives on interface B, but the unicast route toward the source points out interface A; what happens?
cards.a: The packet fails the RPF check and is dropped; multicast is only accepted from the source-facing interface.

cards.q: Summarize multicast routing at a glance.
cards.a: Core is RPF, based on the unicast RIB; entries are (*,G) and (S,G); PIM handles forwarding; MBGP carries multicast NLRIs (SAFI 2); MSDP handles RP discovery; SSM is source-driven; verify with show ip mroute.
